# infrawrench_deploy_trigger (Resource)

Redeploys a repository's environment when its branch moves.

`enabled` is the **only** mutable field: repo, branch, environment and the stored deploy answers are all fixed at creation, so changing any of them replaces the trigger. That is the API's shape rather than a choice here, and it is a reasonable one — a trigger pointed at a different branch is a different trigger.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `branch` (String) Branch to watch. A push to it starts a deploy.
- `env` (String) Environment to deploy into, e.g. `production`.
- `repo` (String) Repository, as `owner/name`. Must be one the connected GitHub App can see — list them at `/deployments/repos`.

### Optional

- `answers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Stored answers to the deploy questionnaire, keyed by question id — the values the plan step would otherwise stop and ask for.

Write-only and create-only: no route returns them, so the provider cannot detect drift on them, and changing them replaces the trigger. Marked sensitive because deploy answers routinely carry connection strings.
- `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled trigger keeps its settings and ignores pushes.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned trigger id. Use it with `terraform import` — though an imported trigger has no `answers` in state, since no route returns them.
- `last_sha` (String) The commit the trigger last deployed, or null if it never has.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_deploy_trigger.example 8e9f0a1b-2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d0e1f2a3b
```
